title: SLO contracting playbook for embedded partner integrations
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook describes how SRE teams partner with Sales, Legal, and Product to negotiate, validate, and operationalize SLOs and error-budget commitments for embedded partner integrations (SDKs, hosted widgets, and partner-hosted Dedicated/Private deployments). It covers capacity evidence required pre-contract, realtime operational tooling, incident acceptance criteria, and a post-incident remediation template tailored to partner SLAs.

Goals
-----
- Create a reproducible, low-friction process for SLO commitments to partners while protecting platform reliability and capacity headroom.
- Standardize the telemetry, runbooks, and acceptance criteria required before any financial SLA is approved.
- Minimize surprise capacity risk and automate evidence collection for quarterly QBRs and legal audits.

When to use this playbook
-------------------------
Use this document for:
- New partner integrations that embed Redwood endpoints behind partner UI/SDK.
- Conversions of high-volume self-serve customers into committed capacity contracts.
- Any contractual SLOs or financial credits tied to error budgets.

Key roles and responsibilities
------------------------------
- SRE (owner): validate capacity proofs, define operational runbooks, onboard partner telemetry, maintain incident templates.
- Sales / Solutions: collect integration topology, expected QPS and traffic patterns, business consequences for breaches.
- Legal: draft SLA language, credit calculations, evidence acceptance windows.
- Product / Partner Engineering: own partner-side fallbacks and integration testing.

Minimum pre-contract evidence checklist (gate)
--------------------------------------------
All items below must be submitted and verified before SLA countersignature. SRE verification must mark each item as PASS/FAIL in the contract ticket.

1) Traffic profile and growth forecast (CSV sample)
   - 7-day rolling QPS/peak, 95th quantile payload size distribution, expected seasonal multipliers.
2) Canary & shadow traffic plan
   - Canary window, sample size, pass/fail thresholds.
3) Headroom reservation request
   - Baseline reserved tokens/GPUs and burst policy (see table).
4) Telemetry contract (events and labels)
   - Required spans: request_id, partner_id, route_id, latency_ms, model_variant, outcome_code.
5) Integration test harness
   - Synthetic trace set (prompt-sets), perf run (90th/95th percentiles), and quality baselines (per prompt-set accuracy or baseline BLEU/EM as appropriate).

Capacity reservation tiers (reference)
-------------------------------------
| Tier | Monthly committed tokens | Buffer headroom | Burst allowance | Typical use case |
|------|--------------------------:|-----------------:|----------------:|------------------|
| A    | 100M+                    | 25%              | 2x for 6 hours  | Large SaaS integrations with strict SLAs |
| B    | 10M-100M                 | 20%              | 1.5x for 3 hours| Mid-size partners with scheduled peak windows |
| C    | <10M                     | 10%              | 1.25x for 1 hour| Low-volume pilots and dev embeds |

Negotiation guardrails for SLOs
-------------------------------
- Avoid single-metric SLAs (e.g., 99.99% availability alone). Use multi-dimensional SLOs: latency, success (HTTP 2xx / model-valid responses), and quality (model regression guardrails).
- Error budget burn formula must account for partner-specific traffic shaping and planned maintenance windows.
- Financial credits scale with sustained burn rate over a sliding 7-day window (not instant spikes). Example clause: 3 consecutive days over 50% of monthly budget -> credit trigger.

Operational telemetry and tooling
--------------------------------
Required dashboards and alerts (SRE provides templates)
- Partner SLO dashboard: 50/95/99 latency quantiles, success rate, tokens consumed, reserve consumption, and canary pass rate.
- Error-budget alerting: warning at 30% burn remaining, critical at 10% burn remaining.
- Capacity saturation alert: reserved headroom < 5% for more than 10m.

Suggested observability instrumentation (telemetry contract)
{"events": ["request_start","request_end","model_load","fallback_invoked"], "labels": ["partner_id","route","model_variant","host_region"]}
(Partners must implement forwarding or agree to server-side token sampling; SRE provides collection endpoints and a vendor onboarding checklist.)

Runbook: partner SLO breach triage (high-level)
------------------------------------------------
1) Acknowledge: Pager duty alert -> SRE oncall acknowledges within 15 minutes.
2) Triage: Identify scope (single-partner vs multi-tenant), failure mode (latency, error rate, quality drift), and impacted routes.
3) Contain: Invoke partner rate-limiting or downgrade to cached variant. If capacity reserved is exhausted, execute pre-authorized emergency burst policy or negotiated throttling.
4) Remediate: Roll forward fallback, scale model pool, or apply targeted admission control.
5) Communicate: Post an initial incident summary to partner within 60 minutes with expected ETA.
6) Evidence: Collect telemetry snapshot, canary traces, and request samples for legal evidence retention (retain for 90 days unless otherwise specified).

Incident review expectations and templates
-----------------------------------------
For any incident that consumes > 20% of monthly error budget or triggers financial credits, the following are required within 7 business days:
- Blameless incident writeup (SRE lead) with timeline, hypothesis, evidence, and remediation steps.
- Partner-facing impact summary (CS + Sales + SRE) for the partner QBR.
- A prioritized remediation backlog item assigned to Product or Platform with a target ship date.

Post-incident remediation checklist (example items)
- Root cause analysis confirmed with traces and before/after telemetry.
- A mitigation (code/config) shipped or scheduled.
- Update to capacity reservation or SLA language if misprovisioning contributed.
- Add synthetic canaries targeted at the observed failure mode.

Automated evidence pack (SRE deliverable)
----------------------------------------
SRE will produce a zipped evidence pack containing:
- Time-series segments (latency, success-rate, tokens) in CSV.
- Sample request traces (sanitized).
- Canary results and pass/fail logs.
- Runbook steps executed with timestamps and operator notes.

Runbook snippet: emergency soft-throttle (CLI)
--------------------------------------------
1) Identify partner scope: 
   curl -s "https://ops-api.redwood.internal/partners?partner_id=XYZ" | jq
2) Apply soft throttle (10m):
   redwood-ctl throttle apply --partner XYZ --rate 0.7 --duration 10m --reason "SLO burn containment"
3) Monitor and rollback:
   redwood-ctl throttle status --partner XYZ
   redwood-ctl throttle cancel --partner XYZ --confirm

Acceptance & auditable evidence for QBRs
----------------------------------------
Before a partner SLO goes live, SRE must sign-off on:
- Canary pass at the configured scale,
- Observability coverage (dashboards & alerts), and
- Contract ticket with headroom and burst policy approved by capacity planning.

Checklist for SRE sign-off (to be attached to contract)
- [ ] Canary run (date + pass/fail)
- [ ] Dashboard deployed and shared
- [ ] Reserved capacity provisioned in billing system
- [ ] Runbook assigned with oncall contacts
- [ ] Legal SLA drafted and reviewed

Appendix: common failure modes and pre-authorized mitigations
------------------------------------------------------------
- Cold-start model latency: pre-warm pool for partner routes (provisioned by Tier A/B).
- KV cache contamination: enable per-partner namespaces and rapid cache flush endpoint.
- Quality regression: auto-fallback to validated model-variant with canary gating.

Maintenance windows and blackout periods
--------------------------------------
- Planned maintenance windows for partner-facing routes must be disclosed 72 hours in advance.
- For embedded partners with financial SLAs, avoid maintenance during declared peak windows unless agreed with credits/compensations.
